verdict.rationale: Unreal documents built-in version-control integration with Perforce and SVN for sharing assets and code across a team, with history and rollback. It also documents Multi-User Editing, which puts several editor instances into one shared live session; that feature is marked Beta. The story's 'built-in collaboration' branch is clearly delivered, but nothing in the pack shows mergeable scenes or diffable text asset formats. Missing for 10: evidence of mergeable scene files or diffable text formats, Multi-User Editing beyond Beta status, independent or hands-on corroboration of team workflows.

support.subject: As a studio lead, the project format and tooling play well with version control and multi-person teams — mergeable scenes, diffable text formats, or built-in collaboration

citations.quote: Unreal Engine comes with two fully-integrated methods that allow people to work together on their projects using version control software like Perforce and SVN.

Source Control allows users on your team to share assets and code with one another, as well as providing a backup and history of changes so any files can be rolled back to an earlier version if something went wrong with the file.
With Multi-User Editing, you can connect multiple instances of Unreal Editor together to work collaboratively in a shared editing session, building a single virtual world together with your teammates
